solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Doctor nearly retiring during great plague

indicators.note: during says one piece sits within the time, here the letters, of the other

parts.note: great in the sense of grand or heroic, epic

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the shortened word is read backwards
nearly says the word for doctor stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: a doctor is a medic

explanation.surface: A doctor about to retire works through a great outbreak of disease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' looks like stepping down from work; here it means read backwards, and 'nearly' trims the doctor first.
explanation.definitionFit: A plague is a widespread outbreak of disease, which is what an epidemic means.

clue.text: Seasonal food that's excellent and poor

parts.note: a plum job is an excellent one
duff is British slang for useless or of poor quality

explanation.surface: A festive dish that manages to be both wonderful and dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: DUFF is British slang for broken or rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Plum duff is a boiled suet pudding with dried fruit, traditionally eaten at Christmas in Britain.

clue.text: Good behaviour missing in pupil

indicators.note: missing says a part is lacking from the longer word

parts.note: orderly conduct is discipline

explanation.surface: A schoolchild who lacks good conduct.
explanation.definitionFit: A disciple is a follower who learns from a master, a pupil in the old sense.

clue.text: Returning actor's seized with kissing sound

indicators.note: seized says one piece grips the other inside it
returning means coming back, so the word for actor is read backwards

parts.note: a ham is an overacting actor; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: A returning actor greeted with an air kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returning' turns HAM to MAH, and 'seized' puts W inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The word imitates the smacking noise of a theatrical air kiss, a luvvie's greeting.

clue.text: The Old Vic performing something woolly

indicators.note: performing suggests the letters are put through their paces into a new order

explanation.surface: London's Old Vic theatre stages a show about something fleecy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performing' rearranges THE, O and VIC; the Old Vic is a London theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cheviot is a breed of sheep from the Cheviot Hills, and its wool and the cloth made from it share the name.

clue.text: Shanghai almost needs a port manager

indicators.note: almost says the word for shanghai loses its final letter

parts.note: to shanghai is to force someone into service, to impress them
Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port

explanation.surface: Shanghai, a great port city, nearly needs another port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shanghai' is a verb, not the city: to shanghai or impress is to press-gang. 'almost' cuts IMPRESS to IMPRES.
explanation.definitionFit: An impresario organises and manages theatrical or musical productions.

clue.text: Small boat touring lake's top

indicators.note: touring means going around, so the boat goes round the other piece

parts.note: a pinnace is a small boat carried by a larger ship
L is an abbreviation for lake; the 's is a link

explanation.surface: A little boat cruising round a lake's summit.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinnacle is the highest point or peak of something.

clue.text: Abroad, I will surmount a terrible resentment

indicators.note: in a down clue, surmounting means sitting on top, so this piece comes first

parts.note: je is French for I
lousy means very bad

explanation.surface: Someone overseas determined to rise above dreadful bitterness.
explanation.definitionFit: Jealousy is resentment of another's advantages or rivalry in love.

clue.text: Crime of America's neighbour probed by police

indicators.note: probed by says the other piece is pushed inside this one

parts.note: homie is American slang for someone from one's own neighbourhood
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of the British police

explanation.surface: A crime in Canada or Mexico being investigated by the police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'America's neighbour' looks like Canada or Mexico; it is American slang for a pal from one's own neighbourhood.
explanation.definitionFit: Homicide is the killing of one person by another, a serious crime.

clue.text: Screen star's taken stimulant

parts.note: the sun is a star; with the 's it gives suns
had means taken, as in had a drink
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A film star has taken drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screen' suggests film and 'star' a celebrity; the screen blocks the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunshade is a parasol or awning that shields one from the sun.

clue.text: Instrument untouched by a learner

parts.note: virgin means unspoiled or untouched
L is the learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A musical instrument that a beginner has never played.
explanation.definitionFit: The virginal is a small keyboard instrument of the harpsichord family.

clue.text: Cynical society promising to depose leader

indicators.note: deposing a leader removes the one at the head, the first letter

parts.note: auspicious means promising or favourable

explanation.surface: A distrustful society plans to oust its head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depose leader' drops the A of AUSPICIOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A cynical person distrusts others' motives, so is suspicious of them.

clue.text: Dancing the can-can, I laugh loudly

indicators.note: dancing jumbles the letters as if they were stepping about

explanation.surface: A cabaret dancer roars with laughter while high-kicking.
explanation.definitionFit: To cachinnate is a rare, formal verb for laughing loudly or immoderately.

clue.text: Pie crust somewhat greyish

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A pastry case that has turned a bit grey.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecru is a pale beige or greyish-yellow colour, like unbleached linen.

clue.text: Misdeed from person selling hot stuff

parts.note: of can mean from, as in a man of Kent
a fence deals in stolen, or hot, goods

explanation.surface: A crime committed by someone dealing in stolen goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hot stuff' suggests spicy food; here it is stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: An offence is a breach of law or rules, a misdeed.

clue.text: Wrongful arrest claimed by large speaker

indicators.note: claimed by says this piece is taken into the other, which holds it

parts.note: OS is outsize, a clothing size for large

indicators.note: wrongful suggests the letters are set out in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A big talker complains about a wrongful arrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrongful' scrambles the six letters to RATRES before they are taken in.
explanation.definitionFit: An oratress is a female orator, a public speaker.

clue.text: Wood collected for treatment

parts.note: fir is a type of wood
collected means calm and composed, staid

explanation.surface: Timber gathered up to treat an injury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collected' is the adjective meaning composed, not gathered.
explanation.definitionFit: First aid is the immediate treatment given to an injured or sick person.

clue.text: Inquire about graceless, stuffy behaviour

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: to pry is to inquire nosily
rude means lacking manners or grace

explanation.surface: Asking nosy questions about rude, priggish conduct.
explanation.definitionFit: Prudery is excessive concern with propriety, a stuffy prim manner.

clue.text: Food with lots of calories for singer

parts.note: diet is the food one eats
rich food is heavy and calorific

explanation.surface: Fattening fare served to a vocalist.
explanation.definitionFit: Marlene Dietrich was a German-born actress and singer.

clue.text: Anarchic sellers tailored stocking for everyone

indicators.note: stocking means holding as stock, so this piece contains the other
tailored means altered to fit, so the letters are refashioned

parts.note: U is the British film certificate for universal viewing

explanation.surface: Lawless salesmen offer made-to-measure hosiery for all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailored' rearranges SELLERS to RLELESS, and 'stocking' holds U inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Anarchic means lacking order or rules, which is what ruleless says.

clue.text: Bird to fight twice

parts.note: to spar is to fight, as boxers do in practice
twice says the idea of fighting is used again, as a row or quarrel

explanation.surface: A bird that scraps and scraps again.
explanation.definitionFit: The sparrow is a small brown songbird common in towns.

clue.text: Insouciant Cockney's dangerous

indicators.note: Cockney speakers drop their aitches, so the first letter is lost

parts.note: hairy is slang for risky or dangerous

explanation.surface: A carefree Londoner who is actually a menace.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney is a working-class Londoner, whose accent drops the H; HAIRY becomes 'AIRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Airy means light-hearted and casually unconcerned, like insouciant.

clue.text: Indecently intimate around cowboy, perhaps

indicators.note: around says one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: to intimate is to hint at, imply
a roper lassoes cattle, as a cowboy may

explanation.surface: Getting too intimate with a cowboy, rather shamelessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intimate' is the verb meaning hint, not the adjective meaning close.
explanation.definitionFit: Improperly means in an unseemly way, and can mean indecently.

clue.text: Servant who could be Eritrean

indicators.note: who could be says the letters could form a different word

explanation.surface: A domestic who might be from Eritrea.
explanation.definitionFit: A retainer is a long-serving servant of a household.

clue.text: Damage statuette with no head

indicators.note: with no head means the first letter is cut off

parts.note: the Oscar is the Academy Award statuette

explanation.surface: Knocking the head off a film award trophy.
explanation.definitionFit: To scar is to mark or disfigure, to damage permanently.

clue.text: Right conman losing diamonds one returns in court

indicators.note: losing says a letter is taken away

parts.note: a conman is a deceiver
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A con artist who lost jewels returns to face trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' suggests a law court; it is a tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis the receiver is the player who returns the serve.

clue.text: Blade twirls at intervals in fight

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a set-to is a brief fight

indicators.note: at intervals says every other letter is picked

explanation.surface: A knife spun now and then during a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at intervals' takes TIL from twirls; 'in' puts it into SETTO.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiletto is a short dagger with a thin tapering blade.

clue.text: Roguish card player's collected funds for campaign

indicators.note: collected says one piece gathers the other inside it

parts.note: West is one of the four players at bridge; the 's stands for has
arch means playfully mischievous or roguish

explanation.surface: A sly gambler has raised money for an election.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the four players are named North, South, East and West.
explanation.definitionFit: A war chest is a fund of money set aside for a campaign.
